about.summary: Each point is one histopathology patch from lymph node sections, encoded by a StyleGAN2 trained with an encoder on PatchCamelyon. 26,542 patches, about half of them labelled as containing metastasis.

sections.title: Source
items: PatchCamelyon (Veeling et al. 2018): 96 × 96 px patches at 10× from the Camelyon16 whole-slide images of H&E-stained sentinel lymph nodes of breast cancer patients (two Dutch hospitals).

sections.title: Model
items: StyleGAN2 trained with an encoder (after Adversarial Latent Autoencoders, Pidhorskyi et al. 2020): the discriminator is split into an encoder and a small classifier, and a consistency loss makes the encoder map a generated image back to the latent vector it was generated from.
Each image is encoded to one latent vector (one point per image), projected with UMAP; the UMAP parameters were not recorded.

sections.title: Colour options
items: label: the PCam label, 1 = the central 32 × 32 px of the patch contain at least one pixel of tumour (from the Camelyon16 metastasis annotations), 0 = they do not. Tumour outside the centre does not count.

sections.title: Caveats
items: The embeddings do not separate the classes: linear classifiers on them stayed at chance level, while groups of duplicates, black patches and patches without tissue form their own clusters (see the blog post).
